weather.tip: 86% rain chance today — carry an umbrella, and build in extra buffer time for your commute since Bengaluru's roads flood and snarl fast once the rain starts.

around.headline: Software professional arrested for secretly filming his landlady
around.summary: A private-firm employee/software professional was arrested after allegedly secretly filming his landlady in the bathroom of the property he rented. If you're a tenant or landlord, be alert to hidden cameras and check rented spaces before moving in.

around.headline: 86-year-old run over by KSRTC bus while crossing the road
around.summary: An elderly man was knocked down and killed by a KSRTC bus while crossing a Bengaluru road. Use pedestrian crossings and signals where available, and assume drivers — especially of large buses — may not see you in time.
around.source: Deccan Herald, The Times of India

around.headline: Cross-country rally organisers booked over registration-fee scam allegations
around.summary: Organisers of a cross-country rally in Karnataka have been booked after participants alleged they were duped on registration fees. Before paying any registration or entry fee online for an event, verify the organiser's credentials and prefer traceable payment methods.

around.headline: Namma Metro Green Line disrupted by a technical glitch; minor fire at Nagasandra station
around.summary: BMRCL confirmed a technical glitch disrupted Green Line services today, and a separate minor fire broke out at Nagasandra Metro Station. If you use this line, check live status before heading to the station.

around.headline: GBA drive to reclaim 750 km of footpaths and auction abandoned vehicles
around.summary: The Greater Bengaluru Authority is reclaiming 750 km of encroached footpaths and will auction unclaimed abandoned vehicles after 15 days as part of a pedestrian-safety and decongestion push. Move any long-parked vehicle you own, or it could be swept up in the drive.
around.source: The New Indian Express, The Economic Times

around.headline: Gruha Jyothi free-power scheme deadline looms as drive hits locked houses
around.summary: With the August 30 deadline approaching, the Gruha Jyothi registration drive is struggling to reach houses that are locked or vacant during visits. If you haven't registered for the free-electricity scheme yet, don't wait for a doorstep visit — check with your local BESCOM office directly.

around.headline: Supreme Court issues new SOPs and compensation framework for 'digital arrest' scam victims
around.summary: The Supreme Court has laid out new standard operating procedures and a compensation framework for victims of 'digital arrest' scams, where fraudsters pose as police/CBI officers over video calls. This should make it faster for victims who report quickly to get their money frozen or refunded.

street_smart.title: A video call comes in from someone in a police/CBI uniform against a blurred background, saying a parcel or bank account linked to you is tied to a crime — and you must stay on camera and pay a 'verification' amount right now or be arrested.
street_smart.based_on: Today's Supreme Court news on new SOPs and a compensation framework for 'digital arrest' scam victims — a fresh, evergreen-list topic not used in the last 3 weeks of briefs.
street_smart.situation: Mid-morning, your phone rings with a video call. The caller, in what looks like a police uniform, says your Aadhaar or a courier parcel in your name is linked to a money-laundering or drug case. He tells you not to hang up or contact anyone — you're 'digitally arrested' — and that transferring money to an 'RBI verification account' right now is the only way to clear your name before a warrant is issued. What do you do?

choices.text: Stay on the call as instructed and follow the officer's steps, since hanging up on police mid-investigation could look suspicious.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. There is no such legal power as 'digital arrest' in Indian law — no agency detains, interrogates, or fines you over a video call, and none will ever ask you to transfer money for 'verification'. The uniform, blurred background, and threat of an imminent warrant are all pressure tactics designed to stop you from thinking clearly or checking with anyone.

choices.text: Ask a few questions to test if he's real, but stay on the video call the whole time to avoid making things worse.
choices.feedback: Risky. Scammers running these calls are well-rehearsed and can answer generic questions convincingly, and every extra minute on the call keeps you inside their pressure script. The safer move is to disengage from the call entirely before verifying anything.

choices.text: End the call immediately, do not share any OTP, bank detail, or payment, and report it via the 1930 cybercrime helpline or cybercrime.gov.in.
choices.feedback: Correct. No Indian police force, court, or investigating agency conducts arrests, verification, or fine collection over a video call. Disconnecting removes their leverage, and reporting fast — within the 'golden hours' — is what lets banks freeze a transfer under the Supreme Court's new framework if you did lose money.

choices.text: Block the number afterward and don't bother reporting it since no money was actually paid.
choices.feedback: Risky. Blocking helps you personally, but skipping the report means the number and script keep working on the next, less-prepared target. Reporting costs a few minutes and helps flag the pattern even when you weren't defrauded.

takeaways: 'Digital arrest' is not a real legal process — no Indian agency arrests, interrogates, or fines anyone over a phone or video call.
If you're targeted, hang up first, then verify independently by calling the agency's official number yourself — never one given to you on the call.

Report immediately to the national cybercrime helpline 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in — fast reporting is what lets banks freeze a fraudulent transfer, and the Supreme Court's new framework is built around exactly that window.

quiz.question: The Supreme Court's new SOPs this week address compensation for victims of which kind of scam?
quiz.why: 'Digital arrest' scams — where fraudsters pose as police/CBI over video calls — have caused massive losses nationwide, prompting courts to push for faster victim compensation.

quiz.question: What caused today's disruption to Namma Metro's Green Line, according to BMRCL?
quiz.why: BMRCL confirmed the Green Line disruption was due to a technical glitch, separate from a minor fire that broke out the same day at Nagasandra Metro Station.

quiz.question: India's ongoing Census phase 2, starting August 17, will for the first time in independent India capture what additional detail?
quiz.why: This will be the first caste-inclusive Census since independence, alongside details like parents' places of birth, and is expected to shape future policy debates on reservation and welfare targeting.

quiz.question: Which Constitutional Amendment lowered India's voting age from 21 to 18?
quiz.why: The 61st Amendment took effect in 1989, instantly expanding the electorate by tens of millions of young voters.

quiz.question: Which of these states shares a land border with Karnataka?
quiz.why: Karnataka borders six states in all — Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Maharashtra, and Goa.
